Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //mvw.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 18 s. 2023 MAR 22 2023 MS. NEMESIA M. NASAYAO, RSW Social Welfare Officer Ill Municipal Government of Sikatuna Province of Bohol Dear Ms. Nasayao: This refers to your earlier letter requesting for this Department's legal opinion regarding the appointment of Local Social Welfare Development Officer (LSWDO) pursuant to Republic Act No. 93441 and on the longevity pay for public social worker as mandated by Republic Act No. 94332. Your letter mentioned that a number of towns in your province have yet to appoint a LSWD officer. Below are the discussion relative to your queries: Appointment of Local Social Welfare Development Officer The position of Local Social Welfare and Development Officer, which is considered an optional position under the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160), has already become mandatory having as legal bases thereto Rule III (j) of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of RA 9344, thus: "Rule 111. Local Government Units The duties and responsibilities of each LGU in the juvenile justice and welfare system include the following: xxx xxx xxx (j) Appoint a duly licensed social worker as its LSWDO, who shall be tasked to assist children in conflict with the law. In provinces, cities or municipalities where there are no LSWDOs, the local chief executive shall immediately appoint a duly licensed social worker as its local social welfare development officer who shall perform the abovementioned responsibilities. Should the appointment of LSWDO result in the excess in the budget ceiling for Personal Services, the same shall be justified in accordance with Civil Service policies;" 1 Juvenile Justice Welfare Act of 2006 2 An Act Providing for a Magna Carta for Public Social Workers "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

xxx xxx xxx Such appointment of a LSWDO was reiterated under Rule 114 of the IRR of RA 9344. thus: "RULE 114. Appointment of Local Social Welfare and Development Officer In accordance Section 16 of the Act, all LGUs, particularly at the provincial, city and municipal level, shall appoint a duly licensed social worker as its local social welfare and development officer (LSWDO), who shall be tasked to assist children in conflict with the law. " Let it be noted that the aforequoted provisions use the word "shall" vis-a-vis the local chief executive's immediate appointment of a duly licensed social worker. Well-settled is the rule in statutory construction that the use of the word "shall" connote a mandatory order. Its use in a statute denotes an imperative obligation and is inconsistent with the idea of discretion. In view thereof, we are of the view that due to the indispensable role of a LSWDO under RA 9344, the latter law amended by implication Section 483 (a) of the Local which only made the appointment of a social welfare and development officer in the municipal government optional. Lonaevity Pav for Public Social Worker As to the issue on longevity pay, your letter did not provide sufficient details surrounding this concern in order for us to formulate a concrete recommendation on this matter. Be that as it may, for your guidance, it is significant to note that public social welfare officers are authorized to be granted longevity pay pursuant Section 15 (d) of RA 9344, thus: SEC. 15. Other Benefits. — Aside from the benefits received as required under existing laws and executive orders, the public social workers shall receive the following: xxx xxx xxx Longevity Pay — A monthly longevity pay equivalent to five per centum (5%) of his/her latest monthly basic pay shall be paid to a public social worker for every five years ofcontinuous, efficient and meritorious sen.'ice rendered as cedified by the chief of office concemed, commencing with the setvice after approval of this Act. xxx xxxx xxx

correspondingly, DBM-DSWD Joint Circular No. 1 , s. 20183 prescribes the rules and regulations on the grant of compensation-related Magna Carta benefits to public social workers, including entitlement to longevity pay. Item 8 relevantly states: 8.0 Longevity Pay (LP) 8.1 Pursuant to Sec. 15(d) of RA No. 9433, a PSW may be granted LP at 5% of his/her current monthly basic salary, in recognition of every five years of continuous, efficient, and meritorious services rendered as certified by the chief of office concemed. The grant thereof is based on the following criteria: 8.1.1 The PSW holds a position in the agency plantilla of regular positions; 8.1.2 The PSW has rendered at least satisfactory performance; and 8.1.3 The PSW has not been found guilty of any administrative or criminal case within all rating periods covered by the 5-year period 8.2 PSWs in the service as of the effectivity of this JC may be granted LP for every five (5) years of continuous service. For those granted step increment due to length of service in previous years, the first LP shall be granted after 5 years from the effectivity of the last step increment. 8.3 The first Longevity Pay, LPI, shall be based on the monthly basic salary, Sl, as of the I-Pl effectivity, upon completion ofthe first 5 years of service as PSW. The second Longevity Pay, LP2, shall be based on the monthly basic salary, S2, as of the I-P2 effectivity, and so on. The total Longevity Pay, LPT, at any given time shall be the sum of LPI up to the latest Longevity Pay, LPn, thus, LPI = (0.05) (Sl) LP2 = (0.05) (S2) LPn = (0.05) (Sn) = LPI+ LP2+ ...L pn 8.4 The latest LP may be adjusted due to any of the following circumstances: 8.4.1 Salary increase pursuant to existing law and executive order issued by the President of the Philippines; 8.4.2 Salary increase due to promotion; and 8.4.3 Salat)' step increment due to meritorious performance, and other step increments authorized under existing laws, except due to length of service. 3 Rules and Regulations on the Grant of Compensation-Related Magna Carta Benefits to Public Workers (PSWs)

8.5 The LP shall be a separate benefit not integrated into the basic salary. 8.6 The grant of LP to a PSW on leave of absence with or without pay for more than three (3) months shall be deferred corresponding to the period of leave of absence in order to complete the setvice and performance rating requirements. 8.7 On or after the effectivity of this JC, a PSW previously granted Step Increment Due to Length of Setvice shall no longer be granted subsequent Step Increment Due to Length of Service in view of the prohibition in Item (4)(d) of Congress JR No. 4, s. 2009. Likewise, a PSW hired on or after the effectivity of this JC shall not be granted Step Increment Due to Length of Service. 8.8 A PSW shall be issued a Notice of LP or a Notice of LP Increase, as the case may be, by following the formats attached as Annex "Al" and Annex "A2, " respectively The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated and our appreciation of the same. Further, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of component authorities and the courts. We hope to have provided the necessary guidance and clarification on the matter. Thank you very much. Very truly yours, B A THORITY OF THE SECRETARY AN TOR R.
